ei.title: 3번: The Difference Between Law and Ethics
ei.subject: 빠른독해바른독해_구문독해_2024

fullPassage: "Legal" and "ethical" are not the same thing. Although they seem similar, what is "legal" is not always "ethical," and what is "ethical" is not always "legal." A society's ethics are passed down from one generation to the next, while laws are created by governments. Laws can be changed based on the decisions of people in power, rather than by the beliefs of society as a whole. Another important difference between ethics and laws is how they are enforced. There are no special authorities who make us follow ethics — they are simply something we learn from the people around us. Laws, on the other hand, are enforced by the government, so people know they must obey them. There are many unethical actions, like charging too much for products or spreading false rumors, that are not illegal. However, if you break a law, you will face direct consequences from the government.

questions.passage: "Legal" and "ethical" are not the same thing. Although they seem similar, what is "legal" is not always "ethical," and what is "ethical" is not always "legal." A society's ethics are passed down from one generation to the next, while laws are created by governments. Laws can be changed based on the decisions of people in power, rather than by the beliefs of society as a whole. Another important difference between ethics and laws is how they are enforced. There are no special authorities who make us follow ethics — they are simply something we learn from the people around us. Laws, on the other hand, are enforced by the government, so people know they must obey them. There are many unethical actions, like charging too much for products or spreading false rumors, that are not illegal. However, if you break a law, you will face direct consequences from the government.
